purpose: Pinned comparison references for the bounded Israel pilot. Israel has no incumbent open tax-benefit engine wired to Axiom; nothing in this file is an executable oracle, and no oracle coverage is declared in oracle-coverage-pending.yaml.

oracles.name: OECD: Tax and Benefit Policy Descriptions for Israel (rules as of 1 January 2025)
oracles.role: Independent narrative description of the 2025 Israeli income tax schedule, credit points, and child allowance. Used to cross-check the hand-derived 2025 fixtures. It is a policy description, not a model run, and it is not law. Four fixture inputs are supplied from it and are labelled as reference values wherever they appear; see docs/ENCODING-GAPS.md.
oracles.document: Tax and Benefit Policy Descriptions for Israel (OECD, 2025) — rules as of 1 January 2025
supplies_fixture_values: additional-tax threshold 721,560 (2025) — by inference from its 50% top band; TaxBEN does not name the additional tax
special basic amount 153 (2025) — diverges from the Wikisource annotation 158

oracles.name: OECD TaxBEN web calculator
oracles.role: Candidate household-level oracle. NOT wired: no automated comparison runs against it, and no fixture in this repository was produced by it.

oracles.name: רשות המסים income tax simulator
oracles.role: The Tax Authority's own public calculator, linked from the consolidated text of ITO §121. Candidate oracle for a later wave. NOT wired and not used to produce any fixture here.

notes: policyengine-il does not exist and is not planned. Divergences from any reference above are recorded in docs/ENCODING-GAPS.md as unexplained, with both numbers; no issue is ever filed against an external reference.
